correctness.rationale: The proof derives all even moments from the independently uniform angular and axial surface coordinates. The second and fourth moments reduce, at fixed positive second moment m, to a strictly convex quadratic on the exact interval 0<h²/m<6, proving the complete sharp feasible range [26/19,12/5), its inverse multiplicities, and boundary exclusions. Exact polynomial reduction yields the rational sixth-moment inverse with denominator at least 660m²>0. On distinct two-moment branches the sixth-moment difference equals (11/945)(h1^6-h2^6); elementary sum-of-squares proves the quantitatively sharp separation constant 220/2527. The original source code verifies symbolic identities and independently performs 48 angular/axial quadratures; finite checks do not replace universal proofs.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural inverse problem for the two-parameter family of finite circular cylinder sidewalls under a geometrically canonical probability law. The exact feasible interval, sharp twofold ambiguity transition, explicit ambiguity involution, rational three-even-moment inversion, and optimal separation constant for the two branches show precisely what geometric information can and cannot be reconstructed from low-order ambient random-chord statistics. The study is neither a cosmetic reparametrization nor an arbitrary finite slice; it supplies a motivated boundary to parameter identification, with no claim of noisy-sample reconstruction or general-cylinder coverage.
